findings.title: closedVolumeRatio still hard-codes a 1-hour candle duration; it is not derived from candlesTimeframe or from candle spacing
findings.trigger: Any future change of the candle interval constant, or an equity session whose last bar is shorter than 60 minutes (for example a 15:30-16:00 closing bar).
findings.evidence: SOURCE: iOS copy line 678 and web copy nucleo/src/shared/20-read-model.js:526 are identical: `return c.v > 0 && (!fin(receivedAt) || c.t + 3600e3 <= receivedAt);`. The generated ios/Bobby/Resources/Nucleo/app.html:1240 carries the same literal. This is correct today only because the transport constant is 1H (NucleoDesk.swift:196 `static let candlesTimeframe = MarketTimeframe.oneHour`; nucleo/src/web/30-web-desk.js:83 `var CANDLES_TIMEFRAME = '1H'`). The claim that closed-volume logic 'uses actual candle duration' is not what the code does, and evidence/chart-timeframe-report.md does not make that claim either. No NaN or zero-division path exists: line 532/684 guards `if (!(avg > 0)) return null`, and fewer than 21 closed bars returns null.
findings.fix: Derive the duration from r.candlesTimeframe via a map (1H -> 3600e3) passed into closedVolumeRatio, or drop the claim from the release notes. No release impact while the constant stays 1H.

findings.title: Overlay gate fails open and the footer shows the analysis timeframe when candlesTimeframe is absent or empty (legacy path)
findings.trigger: A reply or re-rendered stored read that lacks candlesTimeframe (or carries an empty string) while provenance.timeframe is 4H/1D/1W.
findings.evidence: SOURCE: line 741 `var timeframe = r.candlesTimeframe || r.provenance.timeframe;` and line 743 `var aligned = !r.candlesTimeframe || String(r.candlesTimeframe).toUpperCase() === String(r.provenance.timeframe).toUpperCase();` (web copy 589/591 identical). With the field missing, aligned is true and the footer is labelled with the analysis horizon, which is the original P2-a behaviour. This is deliberate and tested (ios/Bobby/Nucleo/tests/chart-timeframe.test.mjs:107-113), and the report admits 'The legacy fallback cannot reconstruct a candle interval omitted by an older response'. Current transports always send the field (NucleoDesk.swift:932; nucleo/src/web/30-web-desk.js:326), so fresh reads are not affected. Whether reads saved by build 62 or earlier are re-rendered through buildChart was not checked.
findings.fix: If every historical transport fetched hourly candles, default a missing value to '1H' and gate on that; otherwise hide overlays when the field is missing and provenance.timeframe is not 1H. Confirm how saved reads are replayed.

findings.title: Chart footer 'as of' uses the open time of the last (possibly still-forming) candle
findings.trigger: Any read taken mid-hour: the footer says 'as of 2:00 PM' while the plotted last close is the in-progress price at, say, 2:47 PM.
findings.evidence: SOURCE: lines 761-763 `var now = pts[pts.length - 1]; var lastTime = new Date(now.t); var asOf = fin(now.t) && !isNaN(lastTime.getTime()) ? lastTime.toISOString() : null;` (web 609-611 identical). `now.c` (line 776) is the last bar's close whether or not the bar is closed; closedVolumeRatio excludes the unclosed bar but the chart does not. The label is formatted in device-local time and the UI locale by whenLabel (ios/Bobby/Nucleo/src/app/40-strings.js:358-365), with the date added when the day differs from receivedAt, so weekend equity reads show the Friday date. The Spanish template 'a las {when}' (40-strings.js:59) reads awkwardly when a date is prepended. The test encodes this behaviour (chart-timeframe.test.mjs:43). The claim 'labels data with its actual last-candle timestamp' is literally true.
findings.fix: Optional: label as bar open, or use min(t + interval, receivedAt). Cosmetic; no release impact.

findings.title: Retained P3 (ii): Trader Land share page sets og:url / twitter:url / canonical by replace-only, so they are silently absent if the app shell lacks those tags; og:locale covers only two languages
findings.trigger: A crawler fetches a shared island URL whose runtime shell HTML has no og:url, twitter:url or canonical tag.
findings.evidence: SOURCE: lines 88-91 define `tag` as `out = out.replace(re, ...)` on an existing `<meta ... content="...">` pattern; line 94 `tag('property', 'og:url', meta.url);`, line 100 `tag('name', 'twitter:url', meta.url);`, line 105 `out = out.replace(/<link rel="canonical" href="[^"]*"\s*\/?>/, ...)`. None of these insert a tag when it is missing. The shell is fetched at runtime (api/trader-land-share.ts:98 `shell = await appShell(originOf(req));`), and no index.html exists in the snapshot (Glob for source/index.html, public/index.html, dist/index.html returned nothing), so I could not confirm which tags the shell contains. evidence/README.md:61 states the shared pages lack them, which matches the no-op path. findings.fix: Insert the tag before </head> when the replace does not match, and add a unit test with a shell lacking the tags. Web/SEO only; no iOS binary impact.

rejectedFalsePositives.counterEvidence: There is no product code for it: `-agent.riskNoticeVersion 6` is the standard UserDefaults argument domain read by AgentProfile.swift:162 `riskNoticeVersion = d.integer(forKey: "agent.riskNoticeVersion")`. The remediation receipt records "productEdited": false. The only launch-flag code touching that key is the reset in BobbyApp.swift:74-79, inside `#if targetEnvironment(simulator)` within the DEBUG block opened at line 48 and invoked only from `#if DEBUG` at lines 17-19. rejectedFalsePositives.claim: ContentView.swift:519 could wrongly block a real user who withdrew consent.

NucleoRootView(options: Self.nucleoLaunchOptions) {}`; ContentView is reachable only in the DEBUG branch at line 127 (StoreShots forces it via `-store-shots`, line 92). rejectedFalsePositives.claim: Division by zero or NaN in the bracket percentage or volume ratio.
